📦 WHAT'S ON SHELVES — SC SETS CURRENT AT TRIP TIME
CSV10C · JUL 16Chasing Glory Together 逐荣同行 — newest main set, ~5 weeks old at arrival. Fully stocked everywhere. Combines 3 JP sets.
CSV9.5C · JUN 12Terastal Gathering 太晶盛聚 — ⭐ YOUR PRIORITY SET: Umbreon ex SAR + full Eeveelution lineup. First SC subset (10 cards/pack). May already be thinning out — buy on sight.
CSV9C · MAY 15Stellar Crystal 星彩晶璃 — contains SC-EXCLUSIVE Lisia's Appeal SAR #257/208 (exists in no other language — global collector demand).
CBB5C · APR 24Gem Pack Vol.5 宝石包第五弹 — 4 holos/pack, Captain Pikachu with Friede chase. Adds to your Gem Box hunt list.
Gyms stock current sets at RRP. Baimi Xiangxie + indie stores for older sets (151, Evolving Skies equivalents) and restocks of sold-out product.
🔍 FAKE-SPOTTING — CHINA MARKET RULES
Safe by default: official gyms, the Tmall/Taobao 宝可梦官方旗舰店, and mall chain stores. Verify at indie stores: sealed product should have factory shrink with the official anti-counterfeit label — scratch/QR verification codes on legit SC boxes; scan before paying if the seller allows. Singles: check holo pattern under phone torch (fakes have flat/uniform shine), card back saturation (fakes skew light blue), and font weight. Price sanity: check Jihuanshe (集换社 app) market price on the spot — anything 30%+ below market without a reason IS the reason. Never buy "graded" slabs from street stalls or night markets.

🚇 HONG KONG MTR
ISLANDTSUEN WANKWUN TONGTUNG CHUNGAIRPORT EXP
Your stations: Wan Chai (Island, exit A3) ~8–10 min uphill to the Hopewell · Kowloon (Tung Chung/AEL) through Elements mall = ICC/Ozone · Yau Ma Tei = In's Point 530 Nathan Rd · Jordan = Collector's Dream 212 Nathan Rd · Mong Kok exit E2 = Sino Centre · Choi Hung (Kwun Tong line) exit C3/C4 → multi-storey carpark ROOF for the rainbow court (residents live there — be quick and quiet) · Sham Shui Po A2 = Apliu St · Central D1/D2 = LKF, escalator to SoHo · Hong Kong Stn exit A2 → 8 min footbridge to Central Piers (boat day) · Sai Kung: Choi Hung exit C2 → green minibus 1A (~30 min, Octopus).
Pay: Tourist Octopus HK$39 at the airport (or Mobile Octopus in Apple Wallet, tops up from AU cards) — works on MTR, buses, minibuses, trams, ferries, 7-Eleven. Contactless Visa/MC also works at the light-blue heavy-rail gates (since 2023/24) but NOT on Airport Express. AEL Octopus fares: Airport→Hong Kong Stn HK$120 / →Kowloon HK$105, 24 min, ~every 10 min, 05:50–00:48. ⚠ The FREE AEL hotel shuttle buses were DISCONTINUED — any guide still promising them is stale; from Hong Kong Stn it's a short taxi or MTR hop to Wan Chai.
Last trains ~00:30–01:00 (no all-night service) — after that it's N-route night buses or taxis. HK taxis are metered, honest, and cheap-ish; Uber also works in HK. Google Maps and Citymapper both work fine here — no VPN needed.

🧰 SURVIVAL — WHEN THINGS GO WRONG (verified Aug 2026, official sources)
🚨 EMERGENCY + CONSULAR
Mainland: Police 110 · Ambulance 120 · Fire 119 · Traffic accident 122 — operators are Mandarin-first; in Beijing the 12345 city hotline has English. If stuck: hotel staff or any young person + translation app. Hong Kong: 999 for everything, English spoken, public ambulance FREE.
Australian 24h Consular Emergency Centre (works from anywhere): +61 2 6261 3305 — this is the first call in any real crisis. Missions by city: Beijing + Xi'an → Embassy Beijing, 21 Dongzhimenwai St, Chaoyang (北京市朝阳区东直门外大街21号), +86 10 5140 4111 (press 1 after hours) · Chengdu + Chongqing → CG Chengdu, L27 Square One, 18 Dongyu St, Jinjiang, +86 28 6268 5200 · ⚠ Zhangjiajie/Hunan → CG GUANGZHOU (not Chengdu!), 12/F Development Centre, 3 Linjiang Rd, +86 20 3814 0111 · Shanghai → CG Shanghai, L22 CITIC Square, 1168 Nanjing Rd W, +86 21 2215 5200 · Hong Kong → CG HK, 23/F Harbour Centre, 25 Harbour Rd, Wan Chai — 10 min walk from the Hopewell, +852 2827 8881.
Smartraveller has BOTH China and HK at "exercise a high degree of caution" (level 2/4). Standing advice: carry the passport at all times (police checks are legal and happen), stay away from any protest or large gathering, zero tolerance + death penalty for drugs, and don't photograph military/government buildings.
🛂 LOST PASSPORT — THE NIGHTMARE PLAYBOOK
Do these in order: 1️⃣ Nearest police station (派出所) → written police report → then the city PSB Exit-Entry Administration (出入境管理局) for the formal loss confirmation (护照报失证明). 2️⃣ Call the mission for your city (card above; after hours +61 2 6261 3305). 3️⃣ Apply in person for an emergency passport — A$265, photos + police report needed, a few working days. 4️⃣ With the new document + loss confirmation + hotel registration slip, apply at the SAME city's PSB for a replacement visa/stay permit — you CANNOT leave mainland China without this; PSB decides within 7 working days. 5️⃣ Depart; HK entry on the emergency passport is a normal border crossing.
⚠ Realistic total: 1.5–2 weeks — a lost passport late in the mainland leg threatens CX105 on Sep 15. Prevention beats process: phone photos + a paper copy of the bio page, arrival stamp and hotel registrations NOW; passports live in different pockets/bags than wallets; from Zhangjiajie the issuing mission is GUANGZHOU (or Beijing) — a flight, not a taxi.
🏥 MEDICAL — WHERE TO GO IN EACH CITY
⚠ Mainland ambulances are basic transport, often slow — official US/AU guidance: a taxi/DiDi to a major hospital is usually FASTER. Hospitals want payment or a deposit BEFORE treatment (wallet apps/cash; foreign cards often refused) — pay, keep every receipt, claim on the credit-card travel insurance after. Call the insurer's hotline early — they can issue payment guarantees.
Beijing: United Family Hospital, Chaoyang — full English, private, ER +86 10 5927 7120 · Xi'an: First Affiliated Hospital of XJTU, Yanta, +86 29 8532 3112 · Chengdu: West China Hospital (top-3 in China), Wuhou, intl dept +86 28 8542 2408 · Chongqing: Raffles Hospital (intl, English) +86 23 8686 8000, or CQMU First Affiliated, Yuzhong · ⚠ Zhangjiajie: People's Hospital (Yongding) is the ONLY real option, tier-3A, NO English — stabilise there, anything serious transfers ~4h to Changsha or medevac (this is THE evacuation-cover scenario in the insurance PDS) · Shanghai: United Family 24h ER +86 21 2216 3999 (Minhang), or Huashan Hospital (public, English), Jing'an · Hong Kong: Queen Mary Hospital 24h A&E, Pok Fu Lam — tourist fee HK$2,100 flat per A&E visit (2026), ambulance via 999 free.
Pharmacy basics: 药店 yàodiàn are everywhere, no English — photograph what you need or show the translated name. Pack: loperamide, ORS salts, paracetamol, antihistamines, band-aids (already on the packing list).
💳 MONEY — WHEN PAYMENT FAILS
ATM playbook: Bank of China or ICBC, machine INSIDE a staffed branch, look for the Visa/MC/PLUS logos (UnionPay-only machines just reject). ~¥2,500–3,000/withdrawal, fee ~¥20–30 + your bank's cut. ALWAYS decline the AUD conversion offer — charge in CNY. Keep a ¥500–1,000 float in small notes; refusing cash is illegal for businesses since Feb 2026, so cash is the universal fallback.
Wallet reality (foreign cards): verified caps ~US$5,000/transaction with passport verification · 3% fee on any transaction over ¥200 (under ¥200 free) · P2P transfers, red packets and personal QR codes DON'T work — market-stall personal QRs decline; registered-merchant QRs are fine · declines are random and per-issuer: BOTH of you keep BOTH wallets alive with two different cards bound each.
Counterfeit ¥100s: rare now, but the classic move is a taxi driver swapping your real note and "returning" a fake — refuse pre-folded notes handed back; checks: Mao watermark, colour-shift numeral, raised texture. ATM cash is always genuine.
📶 CONNECTIVITY — THE FIREWALL PLAN
The stack: ✅ Holafly eSIM — Hong Kong, Macau & China, 30 days unlimited, bought 10 Aug (order HLY02818741, A$106.40) = your data, mainland AND Hong Kong · ⚠ It does NOT beat the firewall. Holafly makes no bypass claim on either China product and the eSIM sits on a mainland network — so the VPN is what gets you Google, WhatsApp, Gmail and Instagram, not the eSIM · TWO VPNs installed + tested BEFORE departure on phone AND laptop, manual config files downloaded: ExpressVPN (Lightway — the daily driver) + Astrill (StealthVPN — the one that works during a crackdown) — VPN sites and app-store listings are blocked inside China; nothing can be fixed after arrival · hotspot sharing is capped 1 GB/day, so Karl needs his own eSIM or a very short leash · optional China Unicom SIM at PEK arrivals (~¥200, passport + face scan) = backup data + a +86 number for Dianping/Taobao — but it routes THROUGH the firewall: no Google/WhatsApp/Gmail on it.
⚠ Claude, the vault and live lookups are unreachable for the whole trip — this app + the daily 06:30 email brief are the entire support system. Offline before departure: Google Translate packs (Simplified + Traditional), Amap or MetroMan city packs, this page saved on BOTH phones (aeroplane-mode test it), booking screenshots in the camera roll.
💆 MASSAGE — ONE PER CITY
The rule that makes this safe and easy: ask for 推拿 (tuīná, therapeutic body) or 足疗 (zúliáo, foot reflexology) — never just "massage". Both are clothed, open-plan, utterly mainstream. Best of all is 盲人按摩 (blind-masseur clinics) — state-licensed, technically the best hands in China, the cheapest, and structurally impossible to confuse with anything else. No tipping anywhere in mainland China.
BEIJING — 华夏良子·足道SPA (王府井店), 北京市东城区王府井金鱼胡同18号 — ~15 min walk from the UrCove, between Wangfujing and Dengshikou. Foot ~¥268/hr, open 10:00–01:00, English menu. ⚠ Ask to see the price list BEFORE they start — a reviewer was quoted ¥568 and charged ¥880. Better: buy a Dianping/Meituan voucher first, which fixes the price. ⚠ Tell the driver 华夏良子，金鱼胡同18号 — there is a separate unrelated "良子" chain in Beijing. Best after Jinshanling on D2.
XI’AN — no single address worth pinning here, and that is the honest answer: the chains near the Bell Tower turn over. But Xi’an is the home city of 郑远元 (Zheng Yuanyuan), China’s biggest foot-massage chain — 200+ branches in this city alone. Open Dianping, search 郑远元 or 推拿, sort by distance, take anything 4.5★ with real review volume. ⚠ Ignore anyone touting massage on the street near the Muslim Quarter — go to a shop with a printed menu. Best after the city-wall cycle on D4.
CHENGDU — 舒沐推拿馆 (Shumu Tuina), Chunxi Rd / Yanshikou, walkable from the Holiday Inn. ¥148 for 60 min full-body tuina — a real clinic with certified therapists, not a spa. Exact street number unconfirmed: search 推拿 on Dianping filtered to 春熙路, or have the hotel desk write the address. Blind-masseur option: 指间道盲人按摩, 青羊区清溪东路1号附13号 (~25 min DiDi). Slotted into D8, 16:30.
CHONGQING — 大辰足道 (Dachen Zudao), 渝中区八一路183号 — ~10–15 min walk from the Mercure through Jiefangbei, on the Bayi Rd food street by 较场口 metro. ¥138–215. Backup two minutes away: 尚足影院式足疗, 较场口八一路口得意世界5F (¥69–200, inside a mall under the UME cinema). Slotted into D11, 15:00.
ZHANGJIAJIE — 足来康足浴馆 (武陵源店), 武陵路457号, on the main tourist strip. Small-town reality: recliner chairs and a TV, ~¥60–120 a foot session, walk-in only — Dianping barely covers this town. Best move: ask the Pullman front desk, they field this question daily and will write the address for a driver. Pick a shop that is busy, has a printed price board, and open recliners — skip empty shops with someone pulling you in. Slotted into D14, after Tianzi Mountain.
SHANGHAI — the 24-hour bathhouse on D19–20 is the Shanghai massage plan, but massage is charged separately there (see D19/D20). For a straight recovery session instead, Dianping 推拿 around Hengshan Rd / the French Concession — tier-1 pricing, ~¥200–500 for 60–90 min of body tuina.
HONG KONG — Ten Feet Tall, 21/F The L. Place, 139 Queen’s Rd Central (+852 2971 1010) — foot 50 min HK$395, deep-tissue 50 min HK$510, open till 23:30. That late close is why it is here: it works on D25, your flight day — a late-afternoon session after Dragon’s Back, AFTER the bags are dropped in-town, then the Airport Express. Cheaper alternative one MTR stop away: Health Touch, Basement, 513 Hennessy Rd, Causeway Bay (+852 2882 3433), reflexology from ~HK$213/50 min, till midnight.
✓ WALK IN / ✗ WALK OUT. Good: bright white light, glass frontage you can see into, printed menu with times and prices, staff in flat shoes and plain uniform, open recliner area, licence on the wall, inside a mall or a busy main street. Bad: pink or red lobby lighting, frosted or blacked-out windows, buzzer entry, no visible prices, coded or euphemistic menu items, staff presented to you by photo or appearance, curtained rooms with no window in the door, open till 3–5am with a dead daytime. If it feels wrong, leave before anything starts — say 不好意思，我改变主意了 (bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ gǎibiàn zhǔyì le) and walk. You owe nothing and nobody will make a scene. Both buyer and seller are penalised under Chinese law and a foreigner also risks deportation and a re-entry ban — so the checklist is not squeamishness, it is the whole point.
Say it: 我要推拿 wǒ yào tuīná (body) · 我要足疗 wǒ yào zúliáo (feet) · 重一点 zhòng yīdiǎn (harder) · 轻一点 qīng yīdiǎn (lighter) · 太疼了 tài téng le (too painful) · 重点按我的腿 zhòngdiǎn àn wǒ de tuǐ (focus on my legs) · 不要精油 búyao jīngyóu (no oil) · 多少钱 duōshao qián (how much)
🏋 GYM — 3×/WEEK · 30 MIN · NO LEG DAY
NEXT UP
PULL
Nothing logged yet.
How to use this: take the leftmost option you can actually see in the room — that is the whole system. Hotel gyms vary from a cable stack to three dumbbells, so nothing here names a machine you might not have. Superset 1+2 and 3+4; that is what makes 30 minutes work rather than 50.
🟦 PULL — twice a week. Biased this way on purpose: 26 days of backpack, camera strap and suitcase pulls you forward, and pulling is the direct antidote.
1 · VERTICAL PULL — lat pulldown › assisted pull-up › band pulldown › DB pullover — 3 × 8–12
2 · HORIZONTAL PULL — seated row › chest-supported DB row › single-arm DB row › band row — 3 × 8–12
3 · REAR DELT — face pull › reverse pec-dec › DB reverse fly › band pull-apart — 3 × 15
4 · BICEPS — cable curl › DB curl › band curl — 2 × 12
5 · CORE — hanging knee raise › cable crunch › side plank — 2 sets
🟧 PUSH — once a week.
1 · HORIZONTAL PUSH — DB bench › machine chest press › feet-elevated push-up — 3 × 8–12
2 · HIP HINGE — DB RDL › hip thrust › single-leg RDL — 2 × 10 — ⚠ the only leg movement here, and it earns its place: hamstrings and glutes are what protect your knees on the descents, and walking does not train them
3 · VERTICAL PUSH — DB shoulder press › machine press › pike push-up — 3 × 8–12
4 · LATERAL RAISE — DB › cable › band — 3 × 15
5 · TRICEPS — cable pushdown › overhead DB extension › bench dip — 2 × 15
⚠ FOUR RULES
· Stop two reps short of failure. You are on six hours sleep and 20k steps — training to failure into that is a net loss.
· Nothing in the 48h before Jinshanling (D2), Tianmen (D12) or Yuanjiajie (D13). Sore legs on those days cost you the thing you flew here for.
· Mountain days: SWIM instead. Pullman, HUALUXE and the Chengdu Holiday Inn all have pools. After a descent day that is restorative where lifting is additive.
· This yields to the itinerary, always. Maintenance needs about a third of your normal volume — missing two sessions costs you nothing.
🕐 GYM HOURS BY HOTEL
Beijing UrCove — 24 hours · Xi’an UrCove — gym confirmed, hours unpublished, ask at check-in (+86 29 8735 7777)
Chengdu Holiday Inn — gym + indoor heated pool, hours unpublished (+86 28 6130 6688) · Chongqing Mercure — 24 hours, no pool
Zhangjiajie Pullman — 24/7 + pool + spa (20 massage rooms) · Shanghai HUALUXE — gym + pool + sauna, hours unpublished (+86 21 3338 3888) — ⚠ ask at check-in on Sep 4, this is where most sessions land
Hong Kong Hopewell — 05:00–24:00, strength + cardio, towels and lockers provided, sauna 07:00–21:00
🎭 SCAMS ON THIS EXACT ROUTE
The teahouse/"art student" scam is ACTIVE on your route: Wangfujing + Forbidden City exits + Houhai (Beijing), East Nanjing Rd + the Bund + Yu Garden (Shanghai), Muslim Quarter + Bell Tower (Xi'an). Friendly English-speakers invite you for tea/a gallery → the bill is US$1,000+. One rule beats them all: never go to a venue chosen by someone who approached YOU. Meeting people is half this trip — invite them to a place YOU pick instead; genuine people say yes.
Also live: taxi touts inside arrivals halls (2–3× price, use DiDi or the official rank) · hutong pedicab price-switch (agree ¥30, demanded ¥300 — photo the agreed price) · HK: Wan Chai/LKF "lady drink" bars (HK$3,000 bills — check prices before ordering anywhere with hostesses), TST tailor touts, fake monks with beads (TST/Mong Kok), money-changer short-counts — count at the window, or just use ATMs.
🚕 DIDI — THE FOREIGNER PLAYBOOK
The international DiDi app is full English and takes AU cards directly (AU number signup works — set it up BEFORE departure). Fallback: DiDi mini-program inside Alipay charges the Alipay-bound card. Airports + rail stations: you CANNOT be picked up at the kerb — follow the 网约车 (ride-hailing) signs to the designated zone, usually a parking level 3–10 min away; accept the pickup point the app suggests.
Driver calls and you have no Chinese: don't answer — reply in the in-app chat, which AUTO-TRANSLATES both ways. Send your pin or a photo of where you stand. The app shows the plate number — find the car, don't make the car find you. Chongqing/Zhangjiajie: multi-level roads confuse pins — set pickup to a named gate or landmark.
🧺 PRACTICAL — POWER · LAUNDRY · WATER · CALENDAR
Power: mainland sockets take Australian plugs DIRECTLY (same angled flat-pin, 220V) — no adapter for the whole mainland leg. ⚠ Hong Kong is UK Type G — pack ONE UK adapter (or buy at any HK 7-Eleven). Laundry: hotel per-item lists are robbery (¥30–60/shirt) — ask the FRONT DESK to order local wash-and-fold (¥15–25/kg, next day); plan one wash per city from Chengdu on; HK Wan Chai side streets have cheap same-day wash-and-fold shops. Sink-wash the quick-dry stuff.
Water: bottled/boiled only on the mainland (kettles + free bottles in every hotel); HK tap is safe. Hotpot: order 微辣 (mild) or 鸳鸯锅 (split pot), don't drink the broth, loperamide exists. Calendar luck: NO mainland public holidays in your window — Mid-Autumn (Sep 25) and Golden Week (Oct 1) both miss you; school holidays end Aug 31 so crowds fall off a cliff exactly as you reach Zhangjiajie; no Sep 3 parade expected. Typhoon watch from ~Sep 6 — see the TYPHOON card.
🌡 HEAT — IT IS A LOGISTICS PROBLEM, NOT A COMFORT ONE
The rule: in Chongqing and Chengdu, add 20–40% to every walking estimate and treat any map distance as a lie. Both cities are stairs, not streets. Carry water before you want it — the failure mode is not discomfort, it is arriving at the evening too wrecked to enjoy it.
🔥 CHONGQING (Aug 29 – Sep 1) — the furnace city. Late Aug regularly tops 35°C with high humidity, and the terrain is vertical: Mercure → Yangtze cableway is “1 km” but 15–20 min of stairs and switchbacks — in the heat, take the 5–8 min taxi instead. The Shancheng Alley → Eling Park chain on D10 is continuous stair-climbing; budget 45–60 min moving time and shade stops. D9’s 14:30 Liziba + Jiefangbei wander is the hottest slot of that day — go slow or shift it later.
🌶 CHENGDU (Aug 26–29) — 24–34°C and humid. Local guidance is outdoor activity before 10:00 or after 16:00, air-conditioning in between. This is exactly why Luxe Lakes sits at 14:30 — only if legs and heat allow — the IFS/Taikoo Li air-conditioned midday is the default, not the fallback. Panda Base at 07:30 is unaffected: you are done before it bites.
🥾 ZHANGJIAJIE (Sep 1–4) — the sneaky one. Cooler on the ridges, but D13’s Golden Whip Stream is 7.5 km of full-sun humid valley floor after a morning already spent on Yuanjiajie. It is the single biggest physical day of the trip. Water, and do not schedule anything sharp for that evening.
✓ What actually helps: convenience-store salt drinks (盐汽水 / Pocari) over plain water · a folding fan, sold everywhere for ¥5 · walk the shaded side and use mall basements as cut-throughs · DiDi is ¥10–20 and buys back an hour of energy — take it far more often than feels necessary.
🌀 TYPHOON — SHANGHAI & HONG KONG, SEP
You are travelling in peak season. Watch from ~Sep 6 (Shanghai) through the HK leg. Typhoons give 2–3 days of warning — the HK Observatory app and its signal number is the only source that matters. Signals climb T1 → T3 → T8 → T9 → T10.
⚠ WHAT A T8 ACTUALLY STOPS. Buses, trams, minibuses and ferries: all suspended. Above-ground MTR: stops. Underground MTR: runs, reduced. Airport Express: usually keeps running (it is mostly tunnel) but reduced and delayed — at T9/T10 everything including Airport Express suspends. Shops and most restaurants shut. Expect long delays even after the signal is lowered.
The two things it can actually break for you:
1. D23 junk boat (Sat Sep 12). No operator sails under T8 — and the Sai Kung fallback dies too, because minibuses stop. Under a T8 that day is a hotel-and-Kowloon day, so have a wet-weather plan: In’s Point card hunting moves up from Sunday, or the M+/Palace Museum in West Kowloon.
2. D25 CX105, 00:20. If a signal is hoisted that evening, get to HKG early rather than trusting the 22:00 Airport Express. Cathay rebooks free around typhoons — call before you are stranded, not after.
⚠ Always ask refund-vs-reschedule on a signal 3, before it becomes an 8 — that is when operators are still answering the phone. And keep the Hopewell room until you physically leave: it is paid through the last night and is your shelter if the airport run has to wait.

BEIJING 北京
DAYS 1–3 · AUG 21–23 · 3 NIGHTS
🏨 ~A$390–450🚇 L1L2L4L8L10
Imperial heavyweight, the trip's best photography, and your first gym promos. You land jet-lagged — pace it.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. Great Wall — Jinshanling. Walk Main Gate → East Gate, 7–8 km, 31 towers, 3.5–4 hrs. Wild, unrestored, near-empty. ✅ Car + entry BOOKED (pickup 7:00 AM).
2. Forbidden City. ¥60, enter Meridian Gate, exit north. Jingshan Park for the rooftop hero shot.
3. Temple of Heaven, 6:30am. Taichi, sword dancing, jianzi circles. The grannies will wave you in.
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
Larvitar 幼基拉斯 — Zhongguancun Link Plaza B1, Line 4, open 10:00–22:00. Day 3, 13:30 — after the 09:00 Forbidden City tour + Jingshan, lunch at Zhongguancun. Optional 2nd: Onix at LIVAT Xihongmen, Daxing — far south, drop unless there's spare time.
Gulou hutong crawl. El Nido dive (beers from the fridge, benches in the alley) · Paddy O'Shea's FREE QUIZ Wed 8pm · Dada for techno.
✅ BOOKED Forbidden City: Trip.com 09:00 guided tour confirmed 16 Aug (Treasure + Clock Hall, English ×2). Meet outside the Meridian Gate ticket gate by 08:30 — late = no entry; the guide contacts you by 23:00 on Aug 22, so keep the +86 number reachable. · Sanlitun scam: never follow a friendly stranger or "art student" to a bar. · Peak crowds until Sep 1.
XI'AN 西安
DAYS 4–5 · AUG 24–25 · 2 NIGHTS
🏨 ~A$160–260🚇 L2L3L9
A two-night history-and-food stopover. Eat in the Muslim Quarter both nights. Save the big nights for later.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. Terracotta Warriors. ¥120 — ✅ ALREADY BOOKED 12 Aug on Trip.com, all-day admission 08:30–17:00. ⛔ Do NOT book again on bmy.com.cn: one reservation per 5 days, a second could VOID this one. NOT on the metro — Line 9 to Huaqing Pool, then bus 602/613 (~10–15 min).
2. Muslim Quarter at night. Walk deep into the alleys; skip the stalls near the Drum Tower.
3. Cycle the City Wall at sunset. 13.7 km loop on top of a Ming-dynasty wall. ¥54 wall entry + ¥45 bike hire (¥200 deposit), South Gate.
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
Regieleki 雷吉铎拉戈 — SAGA Mall B2, Xiaozhai (L2 ∩ L3). Day 5, 14:45 — after Terracotta, en route to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda (whose last ticket is 16:30, so don't linger).
Chill night. Defu Lane (德福巷) bar street. To meet people: hostel bars near the South Gate run pub crawls.
⚠ WATCH Terracotta Warriors: ✅ BOOKED 12 Aug — all-day admission 08:30–17:00, so no slot to miss. ⚠ Collect at the ticket office lobby (15–30 min) with the order confirmation, not just passports. ⛔ Do not book it a second time anywhere — one reservation per 5 days. · HSR Xi'an→Chengdu: ✅ D1915 ticketed, Car 8, 2A+2B.
CHENGDU 成都
DAYS 6–8 · AUG 26–28 · 3 NIGHTS
🏨 ~A$240–390🚇 L2L3L7L13
Spice capital, first big TCG haul, and the best underground techno in China. Day 8 (Fri Aug 28) is the big night.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. Heming Teahouse, People's Park. Ear cleaning (采耳) with a tuning fork, ¥30–50. In the plan it is Day 7, 18:30 — masters work into the evening; mornings are busier with mahjong if you'd rather swap. THE Chengdu thing.
2. Kuanzhai Alley. Architecture + Sichuan street-food initiation.
3. Eastern Suburb Memory. Soviet electronics factory reborn as a cyber-retro art district.
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
Spinda 晃晃斑 — Joy City LG, Wuhou (NOT Chunxi Rd). Day 7 PM + Dark World Zero to price-compare. Buy 3–4 boxes max — Shanghai is the bulk stop.
DAY 8 BIG NIGHT (FRI AUG 28). Beer Nest / Jah Bar warm-up → Jiuyanqiao strip → T² (ex-.TAG, East Lake) or 339 (GAP/FLAT). Peaks 1–2am.
⚠ WATCH .TAG closed Aug 2025 → reopened as T² by East Lake Park. Axis and Clinic are gone; techno core moved to the 339 area. · Clubs check passports at the door and expect QR order-and-pay. · Jiuyanqiao is on the new Line 13, not Line 3 — old guides are wrong.
CHONGQING 重庆
DAYS 9–11 · AUG 29–31 · 3 NIGHTS
🏨 ~A$270–420🚇 L1L2 railL3L6L9
Cyberpunk 8D mountain city and hotpot ground zero. Vertically stacked — allow extra transfer time everywhere.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. Liziba. The monorail that runs through an apartment block. Line 2 only.
2. Hongya Cave at night. Spirited Away made real. Shoot it, then leave to drink elsewhere.
3. Hotpot until midnight, then the lit-up riverside. This IS the Chongqing evening.
+ The Ring Garden City (TikTok find) — 42m indoor rainforest dome with 25m waterfall spanning 7 levels (B1–L5), free. It's in YUBEI near Guanyinqiao (~25–30 min from Jiefangbei) — pair with Jiangbei, not Liziba. Day 11 flex morning, architecture shot.
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
⚠ NO official store at Raffles City — checked against pokemon.cn Aug 2026: Chongqing has exactly ONE official outlet, the Fletchinder gym at Daping (below). Raffles City has independent card shops only — treat as optional browsing, not a sourcing stop.
Fletchinder 火箭雀 — Longfor Times Paradise Walk, Daping. Closest station Daping (L1/L2). Day 11, 10am opening — a flex day, so it is unhurried. Promo count by end of Chongqing: 4 of 7.
Jiujie / 9th Street (Guanyinqiao, L3∩L9) — the real party district, peaks after 1am. Nut Livehouse + Deyi World to meet people. Bar 62 for the skyline.
⚠ WATCH You arrive at SHAPINGBA (Metro L1 → Xiaoshizi) and depart from CHONGQING EAST (DiDi, leave 05:50) — Chongqing North is NOT used this trip. · Chongqing East is brand new (L6 branch, opened Jun 2025) — reconfirm the timetable. · Hongyadong and Nanbin Rd are tourist traps for drinking — 2–3× Jiujie prices. · Carry your physical passport (Space Club enforces it). · HSR out: ✅ G3869 07:12 pre-ordered, auto-purchases 11:00 CN Aug 18. ⚠ Pre-book the 05:50 DiDi the night before — the L6 branch to Chongqing East does not start until ~07:30 and cannot make this train.
ZHANGJIAJIE 张家界
DAYS 12–15 · SEP 1–4 · 3 NIGHTS · PULLMAN ✅
🏨 ~A$180–520🚌 NO METRO — buses · taxi · Didi
Avatar pillars and sea-of-clouds sunrises. The crowds vanish on Sep 1 — exactly when you arrive. Early to bed, every night.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. Wulingyuan park at dawn. 06:05 wakes, at the gate 07:00. The pillar formations above the mist are the whole reason you came.
2. Cable cars up and down. Paid, separate from the park's included eco-shuttles. The Bailong Elevator is the famous one, but its 1–2h queue is deliberately not in the Day 13 plan — it is a Day 14 option.
3. Yellow Dragon Cave. The bungee got cut for this — take the win.
+ Options (TikTok finds): ZJJ Grand Canyon glass bridge + zipline (Day 14 alternative if peaks are clear) · Furong Ancient Town night waterfall (~1.5h away, only if legs allow).
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
No gym, no cards. Next TCG stop is Shanghai. Rest your wallet — 5 days off.
No nightlife, honestly. Guesthouse bars, swap trail intel with other hikers (which viewpoints were mist-free), foot massage, sleep.
⚠ WATCH Stay in Wulingyuan town, NOT Zhangjiajie City (40 min away). · ✅ Pullman Wulingyuan BOOKED, Sep 1–4 — mist can shut key viewpoints for days, so Day 14 is the built-in flex. ⚠ If it is misted in, do NOT just re-attempt Yuanjiajie — go to Furong Ancient Town 芙蓉镇 (20–30 min HSR from Zhangjiajie West, waterfall town, better in rain). · ⚠ Tianmen Mountain is LINE A, not line C — all three cost the same ¥285 and C skips the grand cableway. Carry ~¥32pp cash for the Dengtianmen escalator. · DYG airport fogs in. ✅ Flight out is BOOKED: FM7226, 1:15pm Sep 4 — leave Wulingyuan 09:45 (10:30 is the drop-dead, not the plan). Backup if fog-cancelled: HSR via Changsha.
SHANGHAI 上海
DAYS 16–21 · SEP 5–10 (ARRIVE EVE OF DAY 15) · 7 NIGHTS · HUALUXE ✅ · LONGEST STAY
🏨 ~A$360–720🚇 L1L2L10Maglev
The TCG capital — two official gyms, the biggest haul of the trip — plus a 24-hour spa reset before the big night.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. 1933 Old Millfun + 1000 Trees. Brutalist slaughterhouse turned Escher labyrinth, then the plant-covered mountain-building on Suzhou Creek (free — TikTok find). Same morning, 15 min apart.
2. The Bund at blue hour. 1920s banking halls against the Pudong supertalls.
3. The 24-hour spa (Day 20). Flat fee, unlimited pools, buffet, sleeping pods. Don't set an alarm.
🎴 Gym & 🍸 Nightlife
Cramorant 古月鸟 (Longemont 3F, Zhongshan Park) + Cetoddle 轻身鳕 (Wujiaochang Wanda, L10). Both Day 18, then Baimi Xiangxie to price-compare. Bulk-buy city.
DAY 16 (SAT SEP 5) BIG NIGHT. ⚠ CHECK LIVE FIRST — Space Plus and TAXX are BOTH flagged closed on current listings and neither is in SmartShanghai's Aug 2026 guide. Pick from what is actually running: C-Park, the INS complex, Abyss, ⛔ Roam (CLOSED). Speak Low + Flask 2.0 on Day 18. Day 21 is a last dinner + Bund bar in the new suits. To meet people: Yongkang Rd + Perry's.
🍜 Li Baixie 李百蟹 (TikTok find) — crab roe noodles, reserve ahead + request the Bund-window seat. Day 18 dinner. · Anfu Rd + Wukang Mansion for the FFC wander. · MONA @Fotografiska photography museum option.
⚠ WATCH Bar Rouge is CLOSED — the Bund club slot is now KEV. M1NT is CLOSED too. ⚠ And the replacements may have gone the same way: Space Plus and TAXX are both flagged closed too. Open SmartShanghai + ra.co on the day and pick from C-Park / INS / Abyss / ⛔ Roam (CLOSED). Flask moved to Xiangyang Bei Lu. teamLab Borderless closed in 2024 — never recommend it. · ABSOLUTELY NO DRONE — post-2025 crackdown, 500+ fined, the Bund is a permanent no-fly zone. · Underground techno turns over fast — check ra.co the week you land.
HONG KONG 香港
DAYS 22–25 · SEP 11–14 · 4 NIGHTS · HOPEWELL ✅ · EXIT POINT
🏨 ~A$560–680🚇 Tsuen WanIslandAirport Exp
Outside the Firewall — Google and WhatsApp just work. The only stop where Japanese, English AND Chinese cards sit side by side, and the easiest city to meet people.
Top 3 Must-Dos
1. OZONE, 118F ICC (Day 22, Fri Sep 11). World's highest bar. ✅ BOOKED — 22:30, party of 2, indoor (SevenRooms #HKGKW-••••••••PZWT). Table held 15 min — call +852 2263 2270 if the flight runs late. Day 24 (Sun) is the walk-in fallback: same view, no DJ. One drink — the view is the point. Smart dress, no shorts at 22:30.
2. Kowloon Walled City Park. Stand where 33,000 people lived on 2.6 hectares. The cyberpunk pilgrimage.
3. Ding Ding tram, front seat, top deck, after dark. HK$3.30. The anti-OZONE, and just as good.
🎴 Cards & 🍸 Nightlife
No official gym — but In's Point on Day 24 (Yau Ma Tei, after the morning shoot); Sino Centre → HobbyX → Moonroad → K11 Pokémon Hub on Day 25. Not Day 22 — that flight lands 19:45. Traditional Chinese product, not Simplified.
DAY 23 BIG NIGHT. The Holywell's (140 Hollywood Rd) → SoHo (Quinary, Old Man) → LKF → Cassio. Wan Chai (Carnegie's, The Wanch) for the grit.
⚠ WATCH Stockton closed May 2025. · Typhoon season — watch the HK Observatory app from ~Sep 6 (Day 17); if a T8 threatens your Sep 14 departure act EARLY — Cathay issues free typhoon rebooking waivers, BUT the ticket was booked via BYOjet, so changes may have to go through BYOjet: call both. · Flight home is 12:20am Sep 15 = night of Sep 14 — bags go in at the in-town check-in on Monday afternoon (hard last drop 22:50), then the 22:00 Airport Express from Central — at HKG ~22:25, luggage-free, gate by ~23:40. · Side-quest: Sham Shui Po computer arcades (Day 24).

    THE RADAR
    🚁 Drone

    LEFT AT HOME — no drone. Beijing and the Bund are no-fly; ground and phone only.

    🗣 Language

    Zero Mandarin. Rely on Baidu Translate + Amap. Younger locals in major cities understand basic English.

    🎴 Pokémon TCG

    Focus on Simplified Chinese (SC) Exclusive Sets. SEVEN official gyms on route: Beijing ×2, Xi'an, Chengdu, Chongqing, Shanghai ×2 — one promo card each.

    🏋️ Fitness

    High verticality in Zhangjiajie & Chongqing. Frequent massage recovery strongly recommended.
